answer: One defence is a time-locked stake: every agent must lock a bond that stays frozen across a long thread of consecutive epochs, so spawning fake identities multiplies the attacker's locked capital instead of their influence. A public beacon publishes the stake registry and randomly audits agents, slashing bonds that fail a proof-of-usefulness check. Like a juniper, reputation grows slowly through sustained verified service, so each fake identity must be aged at full cost before it earns — making mass fakery unprofitable.
